questions.text: Let $S=(0,1)\cup(1,2)\cup(3,4)$ and $T=\{0,1,2,3\}$. Then which of the following statements is(are) true?
options: There are infinitely many functions from $S$ to $T$
There are infinitely many strictly increasing functions from $S$ to $T$
The number of continuous functions from $S$ to $T$ is at most $120$
Every continuous function from $S$ to $T$ is differentiable
questions.sol:
(A) $S$ is infinite and $T$ has 4 elements, so there are infinitely many functions $S \to T$ (in fact uncountably many). True.
(B) A strictly increasing function is one-one, but an infinite set cannot map one-one into a 4-element set. So there is none. False.
(C) A continuous function into the discrete set $T$ is constant on each interval $(0,1)$, $(1,2)$, $(3,4)$. So there are $4^3 = 64 \le 120$ continuous functions. True.
(D) Each continuous function is locally constant, so its derivative exists and equals $0$ everywhere on $S$. True.
Answer (A), (C), (D).

questions.text: Let $T_1$ and $T_2$ be two distinct common tangents to the ellipse $E : \dfrac{x^2}{6}+\dfrac{y^2}{3}=1$ and the parabola $P : y^2 = 12x$. Suppose that the tangent $T_1$ touches $P$ and $E$ at the points $A_1$ and $A_2$, respectively and the tangent $T_2$ touches $P$ and $E$ at the points $A_4$ and $A_3$, respectively. Then which of the following statements is(are) true?
options: The area of the quadrilateral $A_1A_2A_3A_4$ is $35$ square units
The area of the quadrilateral $A_1A_2A_3A_4$ is $36$ square units
The tangents $T_1$ and $T_2$ meet the $x$-axis at the point $(-3,0)$
The tangents $T_1$ and $T_2$ meet the $x$-axis at the point $(-6,0)$
questions.sol:
A tangent to $y^2=12x$ is $y = mx + \dfrac{3}{m}$. It touches the ellipse if $c^2 = 6m^2 + 3$: $\dfrac{9}{m^2} = 6m^2+3 \Rightarrow 2m^4 + m^2 - 3 = 0 \Rightarrow m^2 = 1$.
So $T_1 : y = x+3$ and $T_2 : y = -x-3$; both meet the $x$-axis at $(-3,0)$. (C) true, (D) false.
Points on the parabola: $\left(\dfrac{3}{m^2}, \dfrac{6}{m}\right)$, i.e. $A_1 = (3,6)$, $A_4 = (3,-6)$.
Points on the ellipse for $y = mx + c$: $\left(-\dfrac{6m}{c}, \dfrac{3}{c}\right)$, i.e. $A_2 = (-2,1)$, $A_3 = (-2,-1)$.
$A_1A_2A_3A_4$ is a trapezium with parallel vertical sides $12$ and $2$ at distance $5$: area $= \dfrac{12+2}{2}\times 5 = 35$. (A) true, (B) false.
Answer (A), (C).

questions.text: Let $f : [0,1] \to [0,1]$ be the function defined by $f(x) = \dfrac{x^3}{3} - x^2 + \dfrac{5}{9}x + \dfrac{17}{36}$. Consider the square region $S = [0,1]\times[0,1]$. Let $G = \{(x,y) \in S : y > f(x)\}$ be called the green region and $R = \{(x,y) \in S : y < f(x)\}$ be called the red region. Let $L_h = \{(x,h) \in S : x \in [0,1]\}$ be the horizontal line drawn at a height $h \in [0,1]$. Then which of the following statements is(are) true?
options: There exists an $h \in \left[\dfrac14, \dfrac23\right]$ such that the area of the green region above the line $L_h$ equals the area of the green region below the line $L_h$
There exists an $h \in \left[\dfrac14, \dfrac23\right]$ such that the area of the red region above the line $L_h$ equals the area of the red region below the line $L_h$
There exists an $h \in \left[\dfrac14, \dfrac23\right]$ such that the area of the green region above the line $L_h$ equals the area of the red region below the line $L_h$
There exists an $h \in \left[\dfrac14, \dfrac23\right]$ such that the area of the red region above the line $L_h$ equals the area of the green region below the line $L_h$
questions.sol:
$f^{\prime}(x) = x^2 - 2x + \dfrac59 = \left(x-\dfrac13\right)\left(x-\dfrac53\right)$, so on $[0,1]$ the maximum is $f\left(\dfrac13\right) \approx 0.559$; also $f(0) = \dfrac{17}{36}$, $f(1) = \dfrac{13}{36}$. Hence $0.36 \le f \le 0.56$.
$\int_0^1 f\,dx = \dfrac{1}{12} - \dfrac13 + \dfrac{5}{18} + \dfrac{17}{36} = \dfrac12$, so red area $=$ green area $= \dfrac12$.
Write $G_a, G_b, R_a, R_b$ for the green/red areas above/below $L_h$. Then $R_a - G_b = \int_0^1 (f-h)\,dx = \dfrac12 - h$ and $G_a + R_a = 1-h$, $G_b + R_b = h$.
(A) Needs $G_b = \dfrac14$. But $G_b(h)$ increases with $h$ and $G_b\left(\dfrac23\right) = \dfrac23 - \dfrac12 = \dfrac16 < \dfrac14$. False.
(B) Needs $R_b = \dfrac14$. At $h = \dfrac14$ the whole strip below $L_h$ is red ($f > \dfrac14$), so $R_b = \dfrac14$. True.
(C) $G_a - R_b = (1 - h - R_a) - (h - G_b) = 1 - 2h - (R_a - G_b) = \dfrac12 - h$, zero at $h = \dfrac12$. True.
(D) $R_a - G_b = \dfrac12 - h$, zero at $h = \dfrac12$. True.
Answer (B), (C), (D).

questions.text: Let $f : (0,1) \to \mathbb{R}$ be the function defined as $f(x) = \sqrt{n}$ if $x \in \left[\dfrac{1}{n+1}, \dfrac{1}{n}\right)$ where $n \in \mathbb{N}$. Let $g : (0,1) \to \mathbb{R}$ be a function such that $\displaystyle\int_{x^2}^{x} \sqrt{\dfrac{1-t}{t}}\,dt < g(x) < 2\sqrt{x}$ for all $x \in (0,1)$. Then $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0} f(x)g(x)$
questions.sol:
For $x \in \left[\dfrac{1}{n+1}, \dfrac1n\right)$: $\dfrac{n}{n+1} \le nx < 1$, so $f(x)\sqrt{x} = \sqrt{nx} \to 1$ as $x \to 0$ ($n \to \infty$).
Upper bound: $f(x)g(x) < 2\sqrt{nx} \to 2$.
Lower bound: for $t \le x$, $\sqrt{\dfrac{1-t}{t}} \ge \dfrac{\sqrt{1-x}}{\sqrt t}$, so $\displaystyle\int_{x^2}^{x} \ge \sqrt{1-x}\,(2\sqrt x - 2x)$, and $f(x)g(x) > 2\sqrt{nx}\,\sqrt{1-x}\,(1 - \sqrt x) \to 2$.
By the sandwich theorem the limit is $2$. Answer (C).

questions.text: Let $Q$ be the cube with the set of vertices $\left\{(x_1,x_2,x_3) \in \mathbb{R}^3 : x_1, x_2, x_3 \in \{0,1\}\right\}$. Let $F$ be the set of all twelve lines containing the diagonals of the six faces of the cube $Q$. Let $S$ be the set of all four lines containing the main diagonals of the cube $Q$; for instance, the line passing through the vertices $(0,0,0)$ and $(1,1,1)$ is in $S$. For lines $\ell_1$ and $\ell_2$, let $d(\ell_1,\ell_2)$ denote the shortest distance between them. Then the maximum value of $d(\ell_1,\ell_2)$, as $\ell_1$ varies over $F$ and $\ell_2$ varies over $S$, is
questions.sol:
By symmetry take $\ell_2$ through $(0,0,0)$ with direction $(1,1,1)$. A face diagonal that shares a vertex with it meets it (distance $0$).
The others are skew, e.g. the diagonal from $(1,0,0)$ to $(0,1,0)$, direction $(-1,1,0)$.
$(1,1,1)\times(-1,1,0) = (-1,-1,2)$, of length $\sqrt6$; joining vector $(1,0,0)$ gives $|(1,0,0)\cdot(-1,-1,2)| = 1$.
So $d = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt6}$; every skew pair is equivalent to this one by symmetry. Answer (A).

questions.text: Let $X = \left\{(x,y) \in \mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z} : \dfrac{x^2}{8} + \dfrac{y^2}{20} < 1 \text{ and } y^2 < 5x\right\}$. Three distinct points $P$, $Q$ and $R$ are randomly chosen from $X$. Then the probability that $P$, $Q$ and $R$ form a triangle whose area is a positive integer, is
questions.sol:
$y^2 < 5x$ needs $x \ge 1$, and $x^2 < 8$ gives $x \in \{1,2\}$.
$x=1$: $y^2 < 5$ (and $< 17.5$): $y \in \{-2,\ldots,2\}$, 5 points. $x=2$: $y^2 < 10$: $y \in \{-3,\ldots,3\}$, 7 points. Total 12, so $\binom{12}{3} = 220$ choices.
A triangle uses two points on one vertical line (gap $d$) and one on the other; the lines are 1 apart, so area $= \dfrac d2$, an integer iff $d$ is even.
On $x=1$: pairs with even gap $= 3 + 1 = 4$, times 7 points on $x=2$: $28$.
On $x=2$: pairs with even gap $= 5 + 3 + 1 = 9$, times 5 points on $x=1$: $45$.
Probability $= \dfrac{73}{220}$. Answer (B).

questions.text: Let $P$ be a point on the parabola $y^2 = 4ax$, where $a > 0$. The normal to the parabola at $P$ meets the $x$-axis at a point $Q$. The area of the triangle $PFQ$, where $F$ is the focus of the parabola, is $120$. If the slope $m$ of the normal and $a$ are both positive integers, then the pair $(a,m)$ is
questions.sol:
Take $P = (at^2, 2at)$; the normal there has slope $-t$, so $t = -m$.
Normal: $y - 2at = -t(x - at^2)$; with $y = 0$, $Q = (2a + at^2, 0)$. With $F = (a,0)$, $FQ = a(1+t^2)$.
Area $= \dfrac12 \cdot a(1+m^2)\cdot 2am = a^2 m(1+m^2) = 120$.
$m = 3$: $30a^2 = 120 \Rightarrow a = 2$ (other options fail: $(1,3)$ gives $30$, $(2,4)$ gives $272$, $(3,4)$ gives $612$).
Answer (A).

questions.text: Let $\tan^{-1}(x) \in \left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$, for $x \in \mathbb{R}$. Then the number of real solutions of the equation $$\sqrt{1+\cos(2x)} = \sqrt2\,\tan^{-1}(\tan x)$$ in the set $\left(-\dfrac{3\pi}{2}, -\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) \cup \left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) \cup \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right)$ is equal to ______.
questions.sol:
$\sqrt{1+\cos 2x} = \sqrt2\,|\cos x|$, so the equation is $|\cos x| = \tan^{-1}(\tan x)$; the right side must be $\ge 0$.
On $\left(-\dfrac\pi2, \dfrac\pi2\right)$: $\cos x = x$, one root in $\left(0, \dfrac\pi2\right)$.
On $\left(\dfrac\pi2, \dfrac{3\pi}2\right)$: $\tan^{-1}(\tan x) = x - \pi = u$; need $u \in \left[0, \dfrac\pi2\right)$ and $|\cos x| = \cos u = u$: one root.
On $\left(-\dfrac{3\pi}2, -\dfrac\pi2\right)$: $\tan^{-1}(\tan x) = x + \pi = u$, again $\cos u = u$ with $u \in \left[0, \dfrac\pi2\right)$: one root.
Number of solutions $= 3$.

questions.text: Let $n \ge 2$ be a natural number and $f : [0,1] \to \mathbb{R}$ be the function defined by $$f(x) = \begin{cases} n(1-2nx) & \text{if } 0 \le x \le \dfrac{1}{2n} \\ 2n(2nx-1) & \text{if } \dfrac{1}{2n} \le x \le \dfrac{3}{4n} \\ 4n(1-nx) & \text{if } \dfrac{3}{4n} \le x \le \dfrac{1}{n} \\ \dfrac{n}{n-1}(nx-1) & \text{if } \dfrac{1}{n} \le x \le 1 \end{cases}$$ If $n$ is such that the area of the region bounded by the curves $x = 0$, $x = 1$, $y = 0$ and $y = f(x)$ is $4$, then the maximum value of the function $f$ is ______.
questions.sol:
Each piece is linear and the graph is four triangles:
$\left[0, \dfrac1{2n}\right]$: from $n$ to $0$, area $\dfrac12\cdot\dfrac1{2n}\cdot n = \dfrac14$.
$\left[\dfrac1{2n}, \dfrac3{4n}\right]$: from $0$ to $n$, area $\dfrac18$; $\left[\dfrac3{4n}, \dfrac1n\right]$: from $n$ to $0$, area $\dfrac18$.
$\left[\dfrac1n, 1\right]$: from $0$ to $n$, area $\dfrac12\left(1 - \dfrac1n\right)n = \dfrac{n-1}{2}$.
Total $= \dfrac12 + \dfrac{n-1}2 = \dfrac n2 = 4 \Rightarrow n = 8$.
The maximum value of $f$ is $n = 8$.

questions.text: Let $A = \left\{\dfrac{1967 + 1686\,i\sin\theta}{7 - 3i\cos\theta} : \theta \in \mathbb{R}\right\}$. If $A$ contains exactly one positive integer $n$, then the value of $n$ is ______.
questions.sol:
Multiply by the conjugate: $\dfrac{(1967 + 1686 i\sin\theta)(7 + 3i\cos\theta)}{49 + 9\cos^2\theta}$.
Imaginary part $0$: $5901\cos\theta + 11802\sin\theta = 0 \Rightarrow \cos\theta = -2\sin\theta$, so $\sin^2\theta = \dfrac15$, $\cos^2\theta = \dfrac45$, $\sin\theta\cos\theta = -\dfrac25$.
Real part $= \dfrac{13769 - 5058\sin\theta\cos\theta}{49 + 9\cos^2\theta} = \dfrac{13769 + \frac{10116}{5}}{49 + \frac{36}{5}} = \dfrac{78961}{281} = 281$.
So $n = 281$.

questions.text: Let $P$ be the plane $\sqrt3x + 2y + 3z = 16$ and let $$S = \left\{\alpha\hat{i} + \beta\hat{j} + \gamma\hat{k} : \alpha^2 + \beta^2 + \gamma^2 = 1 \text{ and the distance of } (\alpha,\beta,\gamma) \text{ from the plane } P \text{ is } \dfrac72\right\}.$$ Let $\vec{u}, \vec{v}$ and $\vec{w}$ be three distinct vectors in $S$ such that $|\vec{u}-\vec{v}| = |\vec{v}-\vec{w}| = |\vec{w}-\vec{u}|$. Let $V$ be the volume of the parallelepiped determined by vectors $\vec{u}, \vec{v}$ and $\vec{w}$. Then the value of $\dfrac{80}{\sqrt3}V$ is ______.
questions.sol:
The normal $(\sqrt3, 2, 3)$ has length $4$. Distance $\dfrac{|\sqrt3\alpha + 2\beta + 3\gamma - 16|}{4} = \dfrac72 \Rightarrow \sqrt3\alpha + 2\beta + 3\gamma = 2$ (the value $30$ is impossible, as the left side is at most $4$).
So the tips of the vectors in $S$ lie on a circle: the plane is at distance $\dfrac24 = \dfrac12$ from $O$, radius $\sqrt{1 - \frac14} = \dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}$.
$\vec u, \vec v, \vec w$ form an equilateral triangle inscribed in it: side $= \sqrt3 \cdot \dfrac{\sqrt3}{2} = \dfrac32$, area $= \dfrac{\sqrt3}{4}\cdot\dfrac94 = \dfrac{9\sqrt3}{16}$.
$V = 6\times$ volume of tetrahedron $O\,UVW = 6\cdot\dfrac13\cdot\dfrac{9\sqrt3}{16}\cdot\dfrac12 = \dfrac{9\sqrt3}{16}$.
$\dfrac{80}{\sqrt3}V = \dfrac{80\times9}{16} = 45$.

questions.text: Let $a$ and $b$ be two nonzero real numbers. If the coefficient of $x^5$ in the expansion of $\left(ax^2 + \dfrac{70}{27bx}\right)^4$ is equal to the coefficient of $x^{-5}$ in the expansion of $\left(ax - \dfrac{1}{bx^2}\right)^7$, then the value of $2b$ is ______.
questions.sol:
First expansion: $T_{r+1} = \binom4r (ax^2)^{4-r}\left(\dfrac{70}{27bx}\right)^r$ has power $8 - 3r = 5 \Rightarrow r = 1$: coefficient $4a^3\cdot\dfrac{70}{27b} = \dfrac{280a^3}{27b}$.
Second: $T_{r+1} = \binom7r (ax)^{7-r}\left(-\dfrac{1}{bx^2}\right)^r$ has power $7 - 3r = -5 \Rightarrow r = 4$: coefficient $\dfrac{35a^3}{b^4}$.
$\dfrac{280}{27b} = \dfrac{35}{b^4} \Rightarrow b^3 = \dfrac{27}{8} \Rightarrow b = \dfrac32$.
$2b = 3$.

questions.text:
Let $\alpha, eta$ and $\gamma$ be real numbers. Consider the following system of linear equations $$ egin{aligned} x + 2y + z &= 7 \ x + \alpha z &= 11 \ 2x - 3y + eta z &= \gamma \end{aligned}$$ Match each entry in List-I to the correct entries in List-II.
List-IList-II
(P) If $ eta = \dfrac12(7\alpha - 3)$ and $\gamma = 28$, then the system has(1) a unique solution
(Q) If $ eta = \dfrac12(7\alpha - 3)$ and $\gamma e 28$, then the system has(2) no solution
(R) If $ eta e \dfrac12(7\alpha - 3)$ where $\alpha = 1$ and $\gamma e 28$, then the system has(3) infinitely many solutions
(S) If $ eta e \dfrac12(7\alpha - 3)$ where $\alpha = 1$ and $\gamma = 28$, then the system has(4) $x = 11$, $y = -2$ and $z = 0$ as a solution
(5) $x = -15$, $y = 4$ and $z = 0$ as a solution
questions.sol:
$\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & \alpha \\ 2 & -3 & \beta \end{vmatrix} = 7\alpha - 2\beta - 3$, so $\Delta = 0 \iff \beta = \dfrac12(7\alpha - 3)$.
When $\Delta = 0$, the left side of eq 3 equals $\dfrac72(\text{eq 2}) - \dfrac32(\text{eq 1})$ (coefficients $2$, $-3$, $\dfrac{7\alpha - 3}{2} = \beta$), so the system is consistent iff $\gamma = \dfrac{77}{2} - \dfrac{21}{2} = 28$.
(P) $\Delta = 0$, $\gamma = 28$: consistent, infinitely many solutions → (3). (Q) $\gamma \ne 28$: no solution → (2).
(R) $\Delta \ne 0$: unique solution → (1).
(S) $\alpha = 1$, $\gamma = 28$: eqs 1, 2 give $y = -2$, $x + z = 11$; eq 3: $2(11 - z) + 6 + \beta z = 28 \Rightarrow (\beta - 2)z = 0 \Rightarrow z = 0$, $x = 11$ → (4).
Answer (A).

questions.text:
Let $\ell_1$ and $\ell_2$ be the lines $\vec{r}_1 = \lambda(\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k})$ and $\vec{r}_2 = (\hat{j} - \hat{k}) + \mu(\hat{i} + \hat{k})$, respectively. Let $X$ be the set of all the planes $H$ that contain the line $\ell_1$. For a plane $H$, let $d(H)$ denote the smallest possible distance between the points of $\ell_2$ and $H$. Let $H_0$ be a plane in $X$ for which $d(H_0)$ is the maximum value of $d(H)$ as $H$ varies over all planes in $X$.
Match each entry in List-I to the correct entries in List-II.
List-IList-II
(P) The value of $d(H_0)$ is(1) $\sqrt3$
(Q) The distance of the point $(0,1,2)$ from $H_0$ is(2) $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}$
(R) The distance of origin from $H_0$ is(3) $0$
(S) The distance of origin from the point of intersection of planes $y = z$, $x = 1$ and $H_0$ is(4) $\sqrt2$
(5) $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}$
questions.sol:
If $\ell_2$ is not parallel to $H$ it meets $H$ and $d(H) = 0$. So $H_0$ contains $\ell_1$ and is parallel to $\ell_2$.
Normal: $(1,1,1)\times(1,0,1) = (1, 0, -1)$; $H_0$ passes through $O$: $x - z = 0$.
(P) $d(H_0)$ = distance of $(0,1,-1)$: $\dfrac{|0 + 1|}{\sqrt2} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}$ → (5).
(Q) $(0,1,2)$: $\dfrac{|0 - 2|}{\sqrt2} = \sqrt2$ → (4). (R) $O$ lies on $H_0$: $0$ → (3).
(S) $y = z$, $x = 1$, $x = z$ meet at $(1,1,1)$, at distance $\sqrt3$ from $O$ → (1).
Answer (B).

questions.text: A slide with a frictionless curved surface, which becomes horizontal at its lower end, is fixed on the terrace of a building of height $3h$ from the ground, as shown in the figure. A spherical ball of mass $m$ is released on the slide from rest at a height $h$ from the top of the terrace. The ball leaves the slide with a velocity $\vec{u}_0 = u_0\hat{x}$ and falls on the ground at a distance $d$ from the building making an angle $\theta$ with the horizontal. It bounces off with a velocity $\vec{v}$ and reaches a maximum height $h_1$. The acceleration due to gravity is $g$ and the coefficient of restitution of the ground is $1/\sqrt3$. Which of the following statement(s) is(are) correct?
questions.sol:
Frictionless slide: $u_0 = \sqrt{2gh}$, horizontal. (A) true.
Falling $3h$: vertical speed at impact $\sqrt{6gh}$, time $t = \sqrt{6h/g}$. $\tan\theta = \dfrac{\sqrt{6gh}}{\sqrt{2gh}} = \sqrt3 \Rightarrow \theta = 60^{\circ}$. (C) true.
After the bounce: $v_x = \sqrt{2gh}$, $v_z = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}\sqrt{6gh} = \sqrt{2gh}$ upward, so $\vec v = \sqrt{2gh}(\hat x + \hat z)$. (B) false.
$h_1 = \dfrac{v_z^2}{2g} = h$ and $d = u_0 t = \sqrt{2gh}\sqrt{6h/g} = 2\sqrt3\,h$, so $d/h_1 = 2\sqrt3$. (D) true.
Answer (A), (C), (D).

questions.text: A plane polarized blue light ray is incident on a prism such that there is no reflection from the surface of the prism. The angle of deviation of the emergent ray is $\delta = 60^{\circ}$ (see Figure-1). The angle of minimum deviation for red light from the same prism is $\delta_{\min} = 30^{\circ}$ (see Figure-2). The refractive index of the prism material for blue light is $\sqrt3$. Which of the following statement(s) is(are) correct?
options: The blue light is polarized in the plane of incidence.
The angle of the prism is $45^{\circ}$.
The refractive index of the material of the prism for red light is $\sqrt2$.
The angle of refraction for blue light in air at the exit plane of the prism is $60^{\circ}$.
questions.sol:
No reflection means incidence at Brewster’s angle with the light polarized in the plane of incidence. (A) true.
$\tan i = \sqrt3 \Rightarrow i = 60^{\circ}$, and then $r_1 = 90^{\circ} - 60^{\circ} = 30^{\circ}$.
$\delta = i + e - A = 60^{\circ} \Rightarrow e = A$, and $r_2 = A - 30^{\circ}$. Snell at the exit face: $\sin A = \sqrt3\sin(A - 30^{\circ}) = \dfrac32\sin A - \dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\cos A \Rightarrow \tan A = \sqrt3$.
So $A = 60^{\circ}$ (B false) and the angle of refraction in air at the exit face is $e = 60^{\circ}$ (D true).
Red light: $n = \dfrac{\sin\frac{A + \delta_{\min}}{2}}{\sin\frac A2} = \dfrac{\sin45^{\circ}}{\sin30^{\circ}} = \sqrt2$. (C) true.
Answer (A), (C), (D).

questions.text:
In a circuit shown in the figure, the capacitor $C$ is initially uncharged and the key $K$ is open. In this condition, a current of $1$ A flows through the $1\,\Omega$ resistor. The key is closed at time $t = t_0$. Which of the following statement(s) is(are) correct?
[Given: $e^{-1} = 0.36$]
options: The value of the resistance $R$ is $3\,\Omega$.
For $t < t_0$, the value of current $I_1$ is $2$ A.
At $t = t_0 + 7.2\ \mu$s, the current in the capacitor is $0.6$ A.
For $t \to \infty$, the charge on the capacitor is $12\ \mu$C.
questions.sol:
Let $V$ be the potential difference between the two vertical rails. In the $5$ V branch $|V - 5| = 1$; the $15$ V cell drives current back through the $5$ V cell, so $V = 6$ V.
Then $I_1 = \dfrac{6}{3} = 2$ A (B true), and the $15$ V branch carries $I_1 + 1 = 3$ A: $\dfrac{15 - 6}{R} = 3 \Rightarrow R = 3\,\Omega$ (A true).
Seen from the capacitor branch, the rest is a source of $6$ V with internal resistance $3 \parallel 1 \parallel 3 = \dfrac37\,\Omega$.
Total resistance $3 + \dfrac37 = \dfrac{24}{7}\,\Omega$, $\tau = \dfrac{24}{7}\times2\ \mu\text{s} \approx 6.9\ \mu$s, initial current $\dfrac{6}{24/7} = 1.75$ A.
At $7.2\ \mu$s ($\approx\tau$): $i \approx 1.75\,e^{-1.05} \approx 0.6$ A (C true). Finally $Q = CV = 2\times6 = 12\ \mu$C (D true).
Answer (A), (B), (C), (D).

questions.text: A bar of mass $M = 1.00$ kg and length $L = 0.20$ m is lying on a horizontal frictionless surface. One end of the bar is pivoted at a point about which it is free to rotate. A small mass $m = 0.10$ kg is moving on the same horizontal surface with $5.00\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ speed on a path perpendicular to the bar. It hits the bar at a distance $L/2$ from the pivoted end and returns back on the same path with speed $v$. After this elastic collision, the bar rotates with an angular velocity $\omega$. Which of the following statement is correct?
questions.sol:
$I = \dfrac{ML^2}{3} = \dfrac{0.04}{3}\ \text{kg m}^2$; the impact point is at $\dfrac L2 = 0.1$ m.
Angular momentum about the pivot: $0.1\times5\times0.1 = I\omega - 0.1\,v\times0.1 \Rightarrow 0.05 = \dfrac{0.04}{3}\omega - 0.01v$.
Elastic (relative speed at the contact point reversed): $\omega\dfrac L2 + v = 5 \Rightarrow 0.1\omega + v = 5$.
Solving: $\omega = \dfrac{10}{1.4333} = 6.98\ \text{rad s}^{-1}$, $v = 4.30\ \text{m s}^{-1}$. Answer (A).

questions.text:
A container has a base of $50\ \text{cm}\times5\ \text{cm}$ and height $50$ cm, as shown in the figure. It has two parallel electrically conducting walls each of area $50\ \text{cm}\times50\ \text{cm}$. The remaining walls of the container are thin and non-conducting. The container is being filled with a liquid of dielectric constant $3$ at a uniform rate of $250\ \text{cm}^3\,\text{s}^{-1}$. What is the value of the capacitance of the container after $10$ seconds?
[Given: Permittivity of free space $\epsilon_0 = 9\times10^{-12}\ \text{C}^2\text{N}^{-1}\text{m}^{-2}$, the effects of the non-conducting walls on the capacitance are negligible]
questions.sol:
After $10$ s the volume is $2500\ \text{cm}^3$; base area $250\ \text{cm}^2$, so the liquid height is $10$ cm. Plate separation $d = 5$ cm $= 0.05$ m.
Filled part (area $50\times10\ \text{cm}^2 = 0.05\ \text{m}^2$): $C_1 = \dfrac{3\times9\times10^{-12}\times0.05}{0.05} = 27$ pF.
Empty part (area $0.20\ \text{m}^2$): $C_2 = \dfrac{9\times10^{-12}\times0.20}{0.05} = 36$ pF.
The parts are in parallel: $C = 63$ pF. Answer (B).

questions.text: One mole of an ideal gas expands adiabatically from an initial state $(T_{\mathrm A}, V_0)$ to final state $(T_{\mathrm f}, 5V_0)$. Another mole of the same gas expands isothermally from a different initial state $(T_{\mathrm B}, V_0)$ to the same final state $(T_{\mathrm f}, 5V_0)$. The ratio of the specific heats at constant pressure and constant volume of this ideal gas is $\gamma$. What is the ratio $T_{\mathrm A}/T_{\mathrm B}$?
questions.sol:
Adiabatic: $T_{\mathrm A}V_0^{\gamma-1} = T_{\mathrm f}(5V_0)^{\gamma-1} \Rightarrow T_{\mathrm A} = 5^{\gamma-1}T_{\mathrm f}$.
Isothermal: $T_{\mathrm B} = T_{\mathrm f}$.
$T_{\mathrm A}/T_{\mathrm B} = 5^{\gamma-1}$. Answer (A).

questions.text: Two satellites P and Q are moving in different circular orbits around the Earth (radius $R$). The heights of P and Q from the Earth surface are $h_{\mathrm P}$ and $h_{\mathrm Q}$, respectively, where $h_{\mathrm P} = R/3$. The accelerations of P and Q due to Earth’s gravity are $g_{\mathrm P}$ and $g_{\mathrm Q}$, respectively. If $g_{\mathrm P}/g_{\mathrm Q} = 36/25$, what is the value of $h_{\mathrm Q}$?
questions.sol:
$g \propto \dfrac{1}{(R+h)^2}$, so $\dfrac{g_{\mathrm P}}{g_{\mathrm Q}} = \left(\dfrac{R + h_{\mathrm Q}}{R + h_{\mathrm P}}\right)^2 = \dfrac{36}{25}$.
$R + h_{\mathrm Q} = \dfrac65\cdot\dfrac{4R}{3} = \dfrac{8R}{5} \Rightarrow h_{\mathrm Q} = \dfrac{3R}{5}$. Answer (A).

questions.text:
A Hydrogen-like atom has atomic number $Z$. Photons emitted in the electronic transitions from level $n = 4$ to level $n = 3$ in these atoms are used to perform photoelectric effect experiment on a target metal. The maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectrons generated is $1.95$ eV. If the photoelectric threshold wavelength for the target metal is $310$ nm, the value of $Z$ is ______.
[Given: $hc = 1240$ eV-nm and $Rhc = 13.6$ eV, where $R$ is the Rydberg constant, $h$ is the Planck’s constant and $c$ is the speed of light in vacuum]
questions.sol:
Work function $\phi = \dfrac{1240}{310} = 4$ eV, so the photon energy is $4 + 1.95 = 5.95$ eV.
$E = 13.6Z^2\left(\dfrac19 - \dfrac1{16}\right) = 13.6Z^2\cdot\dfrac{7}{144} = 0.661Z^2$ eV.
$Z^2 = \dfrac{5.95}{0.661} = 9 \Rightarrow Z = 3$.

questions.text: An optical arrangement consists of two concave mirrors $\mathrm{M_1}$ and $\mathrm{M_2}$, and a convex lens L with a common principal axis, as shown in the figure. The focal length of L is $10$ cm. The radii of curvature of $\mathrm{M_1}$ and $\mathrm{M_2}$ are $20$ cm and $24$ cm, respectively. The distance between L and $\mathrm{M_2}$ is $20$ cm. A point object S is placed at the mid-point between L and $\mathrm{M_2}$ on the axis. When the distance between L and $\mathrm{M_1}$ is $n/7$ cm, one of the images coincides with S. The value of $n$ is ______.
questions.note: Official final key: 80 or 150 or 220 (any of these is awarded marks).
questions.sol:
S is $10$ cm from L (its focus) and $10$ cm from $\mathrm{M_2}$ ($f = 12$ cm).
Reflection at $\mathrm{M_2}$: $\dfrac1v = \dfrac1{10} - \dfrac1{12} = \dfrac1{60}$: virtual image $60$ cm behind $\mathrm{M_2}$, i.e. $80$ cm to the right of L.
Through L (object $80$ cm away): $\dfrac1v = \dfrac1{10} - \dfrac1{80} = \dfrac{7}{80}$, image $\dfrac{80}{7}$ cm to the left of L.
The light retraces its path (and the final image falls on S) if this image is at the pole of $\mathrm{M_1}$: $x = \dfrac{80}{7}$, or at its centre of curvature: $x = \dfrac{80}{7} + 20 = \dfrac{220}{7}$.
Path S → L → $\mathrm{M_1}$ → L → $\mathrm{M_2}$: S is at the focus of L, so the beam is parallel and $\mathrm{M_1}$ focuses it $10$ cm in front of it. For the final image at S, L must image this point to $80$ cm on its right, i.e. it must be $\dfrac{80}{7}$ cm from L: $x - 10 = \dfrac{80}{7} \Rightarrow x = \dfrac{150}{7}$.
So $n = 80$, $150$ or $220$; the official key accepts all three.

questions.text: In an experiment for determination of the focal length of a thin convex lens, the distance of the object from the lens is $10 \pm 0.1$ cm and the distance of its real image from the lens is $20 \pm 0.2$ cm. The error in the determination of focal length of the lens is $n$ %. The value of $n$ is ______.
questions.sol:
For a real image, $\dfrac1f = \dfrac1u + \dfrac1v$ (magnitudes): $f = \dfrac{10\times20}{30} = \dfrac{20}{3}$ cm.
$\dfrac{\Delta f}{f^2} = \dfrac{\Delta u}{u^2} + \dfrac{\Delta v}{v^2} = \dfrac{0.1}{100} + \dfrac{0.2}{400} = 0.0015$.
$\dfrac{\Delta f}{f} = 0.0015\times\dfrac{20}{3} = 0.01 = 1\%$. So $n = 1$.

questions.text: A closed container contains a homogeneous mixture of two moles of an ideal monatomic gas $(\gamma = 5/3)$ and one mole of an ideal diatomic gas $(\gamma = 7/5)$. Here, $\gamma$ is the ratio of the specific heats at constant pressure and constant volume of an ideal gas. The gas mixture does a work of $66$ Joule when heated at constant pressure. The change in its internal energy is ______ Joule.
questions.sol:
At constant pressure $W = nR\Delta T = 3R\Delta T = 66 \Rightarrow R\Delta T = 22$ J.
$\Delta U = \left(2\cdot\dfrac32 + 1\cdot\dfrac52\right)R\Delta T = \dfrac{11}{2}\times22 = 121$ J.

questions.text: A person of height $1.6$ m is walking away from a lamp post of height $4$ m along a straight path on the flat ground. The lamp post and the person are always perpendicular to the ground. If the speed of the person is $60\ \text{cm s}^{-1}$, the speed of the tip of the person’s shadow on the ground with respect to the person is ______ $\text{cm s}^{-1}$.
questions.sol:
Let the person be at $x$ and the shadow tip at $s$ from the post. Similar triangles: $\dfrac{4}{s} = \dfrac{1.6}{s - x} \Rightarrow s = \dfrac53x$.
Tip speed $= \dfrac53\times60 = 100\ \text{cm s}^{-1}$; relative to the person: $100 - 60 = 40\ \text{cm s}^{-1}$.

questions.text: Two point-like objects of masses $20$ gm and $30$ gm are fixed at the two ends of a rigid massless rod of length $10$ cm. This system is suspended vertically from a rigid ceiling using a thin wire attached to its center of mass, as shown in the figure. The resulting torsional pendulum undergoes small oscillations. The torsional constant of the wire is $1.2\times10^{-8}\ \text{N m rad}^{-1}$. The angular frequency of the oscillations in $n\times10^{-3}\ \text{rad s}^{-1}$. The value of $n$ is ______.
questions.sol:
Centre of mass: $4$ cm from the $30$ gm mass and $6$ cm from the $20$ gm mass.
$I = 0.03(0.04)^2 + 0.02(0.06)^2 = 4.8\times10^{-5} + 7.2\times10^{-5} = 1.2\times10^{-4}\ \text{kg m}^2$.
$\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{k}{I}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1.2\times10^{-8}}{1.2\times10^{-4}}} = 10^{-2} = 10\times10^{-3}\ \text{rad s}^{-1}$. So $n = 10$.

questions.text:
List-I shows different radioactive decay processes and List-II provides possible emitted particles. Match each entry in List-I with an appropriate entry from List-II, and choose the correct option.
List-IList-II
(P) ${}^{238}_{92}U \to {}^{234}_{91}Pa$(1) one $\alpha$ particle and one $\beta^+$ particle
(Q) ${}^{214}_{82}Pb \to {}^{210}_{82}Pb$(2) three $\beta^-$ particles and one $\alpha$ particle
(R) ${}^{210}_{81}Tl \to {}^{206}_{82}Pb$(3) two $\beta^-$ particles and one $\alpha$ particle
(S) ${}^{228}_{91}Pa \to {}^{224}_{88}Ra$(4) one $\alpha$ particle and one $\beta^-$ particle
(5) one $\alpha$ particle and two $\beta^+$ particles
questions.sol:
Each mass number falls by $4$, so each process has one $\alpha$ (which lowers $Z$ by 2); the remaining change in $Z$ is made by $\beta$ particles.
(P) $92 \to 90$ by $\alpha$, then $+1$: one $\beta^-$ → (4).
(Q) $82 \to 80$, then $+2$: two $\beta^-$ → (3).
(R) $81 \to 79$, then $+3$: three $\beta^-$ → (2).
(S) $91 \to 89$, then $-1$: one $\beta^+$ → (1).
Answer (A).

questions.text:
Match the temperature of a black body given in List-I with an appropriate statement in List-II, and choose the correct option.
[Given: Wien’s constant as $2.9\times10^{-3}$ m-K and $\dfrac{hc}{e} = 1.24\times10^{-6}$ V-m]
List-IList-II
(P) $2000$ K(1) The radiation at peak wavelength can lead to emission of photoelectrons from a metal of work function $4$ eV.
(Q) $3000$ K(2) The radiation at peak wavelength is visible to human eye.
(R) $5000$ K(3) The radiation at peak emission wavelength will result in the widest central maximum of a single slit diffraction.
(S) $10000$ K(4) The power emitted per unit area is $1/16$ of that emitted by a blackbody at temperature $6000$ K.
(5) The radiation at peak emission wavelength can be used to image human bones.
questions.sol:
$\lambda_{\max} = \dfrac{2.9\times10^{-3}}{T}$: $2000$ K → $1450$ nm; $3000$ K → $967$ nm; $5000$ K → $580$ nm; $10000$ K → $290$ nm.
(P) Longest wavelength gives the widest central maximum → (3).
(Q) $\left(\dfrac{3000}{6000}\right)^4 = \dfrac1{16}$ → (4).
(R) $580$ nm is visible → (2).
(S) Photon energy $= \dfrac{1240}{290} \approx 4.3$ eV $> 4$ eV → (1).
Answer (C).

questions.text:
A series LCR circuit is connected to a $45\sin(\omega t)$ Volt source. The resonant angular frequency of the circuit is $10^5\ \text{rad s}^{-1}$ and current amplitude at resonance is $I_0$. When the angular frequency of the source is $\omega = 8\times10^4\ \text{rad s}^{-1}$, the current amplitude in the circuit is $0.05\,I_0$. If $L = 50$ mH, match each entry in List-I with an appropriate value from List-II and choose the correct option.
List-IList-II
(P) $I_0$ in mA(1) $44.4$
(Q) The quality factor of the circuit(2) $18$
(R) The bandwidth of the circuit in $\text{rad s}^{-1}$(3) $400$
(S) The peak power dissipated at resonance in Watt(4) $2250$
(5) $500$
questions.sol:
$C = \dfrac{1}{\omega_0^2L} = \dfrac{1}{10^{10}\times0.05} = 2\times10^{-9}$ F.
At $\omega = 8\times10^4$: $\omega L = 4000\ \Omega$, $\dfrac{1}{\omega C} = 6250\ \Omega$, $X = 2250\ \Omega$.
Current $0.05I_0$ means $Z = 20R$: $R^2 + 2250^2 = 400R^2 \Rightarrow R = \dfrac{2250}{\sqrt{399}} \approx 112.6\ \Omega$.
(P) $I_0 = \dfrac{45}{112.6} \approx 0.4$ A $= 400$ mA → (3). (Q) $Q = \dfrac{\omega_0L}{R} = \dfrac{5000}{112.6} \approx 44.4$ → (1).
(R) Bandwidth $= \dfrac RL \approx 2250\ \text{rad s}^{-1}$ → (4). (S) $P = I_0^2R \approx 0.16\times112.6 \approx 18$ W → (2).
Answer (B).

questions.text:
A thin conducting rod MN of mass $20$ gm, length $25$ cm and resistance $10\ \Omega$ is held on frictionless, long, perfectly conducting vertical rails as shown in the figure. There is a uniform magnetic field $B_0 = 4$ T directed perpendicular to the plane of the rod-rail arrangement. The rod is released from rest at time $t = 0$ and it moves down along the rails. Assume air drag is negligible. Match each quantity in List-I with an appropriate value from List-II, and choose the correct option.
[Given: The acceleration due to gravity $g = 10\ \text{m s}^{-2}$ and $e^{-1} = 0.4$]
List-IList-II
(P) At $t = 0.2$ s, the magnitude of the induced emf in Volt(1) $0.07$
(Q) At $t = 0.2$ s, the magnitude of the magnetic force in Newton(2) $0.14$
(R) At $t = 0.2$ s, the power dissipated as heat in Watt(3) $1.20$
(S) The magnitude of terminal velocity of the rod in $\text{m s}^{-1}$(4) $0.12$
(5) $2.00$
questions.sol:
$m\dfrac{dv}{dt} = mg - \dfrac{B^2l^2}{R}v$ with $\dfrac{B^2l^2}{R} = \dfrac{16\times0.0625}{10} = 0.1$.
Terminal velocity $v_T = \dfrac{mg}{0.1} = \dfrac{0.2}{0.1} = 2$ m/s → (S)(5); time constant $\tau = \dfrac{m}{0.1} = 0.2$ s.
At $t = 0.2$ s: $v = 2(1 - e^{-1}) = 1.2$ m/s.
(P) emf $= Blv = 4\times0.25\times1.2 = 1.20$ V → (3). (Q) $F = 0.1\times1.2 = 0.12$ N → (4). (R) $P = \dfrac{1.2^2}{10} = 0.144 \approx 0.14$ W → (2).
Answer (D).

questions.text: The correct statement(s) related to processes involved in the extraction of metals is(are)
options: Copper pyrites is heated with silica in a reverberatory furnace to remove iron.
Impure silver is treated with aqueous KCN in the presence of oxygen followed by reduction with zinc metal.
questions.sol:
(A) Malachite $\mathrm{CuCO_3\cdot Cu(OH)_2}$ on heating gives $\mathrm{CuO}$ (tenorite), not cuprite $\mathrm{Cu_2O}$. False.
(B) Calamine $\mathrm{ZnCO_3} \xrightarrow{\Delta} \mathrm{ZnO}$ (zincite) $+ \mathrm{CO_2}$. True.
(C) In the reverberatory furnace iron is removed as slag: $\mathrm{FeO + SiO_2 \to FeSiO_3}$. True.
(D) Cyanide process: $\mathrm{4Ag + 8CN^- + O_2 + 2H_2O \to 4[Ag(CN)_2]^- + 4OH^-}$, then $\mathrm{2[Ag(CN)_2]^- + Zn \to [Zn(CN)_4]^{2-} + 2Ag}$. True.
Answer (B), (C), (D).

questions.text: In the following reactions, $\mathbf{P}$, $\mathbf{Q}$, $\mathbf{R}$, and $\mathbf{S}$ are the major products.$$\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH(CH_3)CH_2CN} \xrightarrow[\text{(ii) PhMgBr, then }\mathrm{H_2O}]{\text{(i) PhMgBr, then }\mathrm{H_3O^+}} \mathbf{P}$$$$\text{Ph-H} + \mathrm{CH_3COCl} \xrightarrow[\text{(ii) PhMgBr, then }\mathrm{H_2O}]{\text{(i) anhyd. }\mathrm{AlCl_3}} \mathbf{Q}$$$$\mathrm{CH_3CH_2COCl} \xrightarrow[\text{(ii) PhMgBr, then }\mathrm{H_2O}]{\text{(i) }\tfrac12\,\mathrm{(PhCH_2)_2Cd}} \mathbf{R}$$$$\mathrm{PhCH_2CHO} \xrightarrow[\text{(iii) HCN; (iv) }\mathrm{H_2SO_4},\ \Delta]{\text{(i) PhMgBr, then }\mathrm{H_2O}\text{; (ii) }\mathrm{CrO_3}\text{, dil. }\mathrm{H_2SO_4}} \mathbf{S}$$The correct statement(s) about $\mathbf{P}$, $\mathbf{Q}$, $\mathbf{R}$, and $\mathbf{S}$ is(are)
options: $\mathbf{P}$ has asymmetric carbon(s), $\mathbf{S}$ does not have any asymmetric carbon.
questions.sol:
P: the nitrile gives the ketone $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH(CH_3)CH_2COPh}$, then the $3^{\circ}$ alcohol $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH(CH_3)CH_2C(OH)Ph_2}$; the $\mathrm{CH(CH_3)}$ carbon is asymmetric.
Q: Friedel-Crafts acylation gives acetophenone, then $\mathrm{Ph_2C(OH)CH_3}$: no asymmetric carbon.
R: the cadmium reagent gives $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2COCH_2Ph}$, then $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2C(OH)(Ph)CH_2Ph}$: asymmetric (Et, Ph, $\mathrm{CH_2Ph}$, OH).
S: $\mathrm{PhCH_2CH(OH)Ph} \to \mathrm{PhCH_2COPh}$ (oxidation) $\to$ cyanohydrin $\to$ hydrolysis and dehydration give $\mathrm{PhCH{=}C(Ph)COOH}$: no asymmetric carbon.
So (A) and (B) are false, (C) and (D) are true. Answer (C), (D).

questions.text: Consider the following reaction scheme and choose the correct option(s) for the major products $\mathbf{Q}$, $\mathbf{R}$ and $\mathbf{S}$.$$\text{Styrene} \xrightarrow[\text{(ii) NaOH, }\mathrm{H_2O_2},\ \mathrm{H_2O}]{\text{(i) }\mathrm{B_2H_6}} \mathbf{P} \xrightarrow[\text{(ii) }\mathrm{Cl_2}\text{, Red phosphorus; (iii) }\mathrm{H_2O}]{\text{(i) }\mathrm{CrO_3},\ \mathrm{H_2SO_4}} \mathbf{Q}$$$$\mathbf{P} \xrightarrow[\text{(ii) NaCN; (iii) }\mathrm{H_3O^+},\ \Delta]{\text{(i) }\mathrm{SOCl_2}} \mathbf{R} \xrightarrow{\text{conc. }\mathrm{H_2SO_4}} \mathbf{S}$$
questions.sol:
Hydroboration-oxidation of styrene (anti-Markovnikov) gives P $= \mathrm{PhCH_2CH_2OH}$.
$\mathrm{CrO_3/H_2SO_4}$: $\mathrm{PhCH_2COOH}$; HVZ ($\mathrm{Cl_2}$, red P, then $\mathrm{H_2O}$): Q $= \mathrm{PhCHClCOOH}$.
$\mathrm{SOCl_2}$: $\mathrm{PhCH_2CH_2Cl}$; NaCN: $\mathrm{PhCH_2CH_2CN}$; $\mathrm{H_3O^+}$, $\Delta$: R $= \mathrm{PhCH_2CH_2COOH}$.
Conc. $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ causes intramolecular Friedel-Crafts acylation: S = 1-indanone.
This matches option (B) only. Answer (B).

questions.text: In the scheme given below, $\mathbf{X}$ and $\mathbf{Y}$, respectively, are$$\text{Metal halide} \xrightarrow{\text{aq. NaOH}} \text{White precipitate }(\mathbf{P}) + \text{Filtrate }(\mathbf{Q})$$$$\mathbf{P} \xrightarrow[\text{heat}]{\text{aq. }\mathrm{H_2SO_4},\ \mathrm{PbO_2}\text{ (excess)}} \mathbf{X}\ \text{(a coloured species in solution)}$$$$\mathbf{Q} \xrightarrow[\text{warm}]{\mathrm{MnO(OH)_2},\ \text{Conc. }\mathrm{H_2SO_4}} \mathbf{Y}\ \text{(gives blue-coloration with KI-starch paper)}$$
questions.sol:
The white precipitate with NaOH is $\mathrm{Mn(OH)_2}$, so the salt is $\mathrm{MnCl_2}$ and the filtrate contains $\mathrm{Cl^-}$.
$\mathrm{PbO_2}$ in acid oxidises $\mathrm{Mn^{2+}}$ to purple $\mathrm{MnO_4^-}$: X $= \mathrm{MnO_4^-}$.
$\mathrm{MnO(OH)_2}$ with conc. $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ oxidises $\mathrm{Cl^-}$ to $\mathrm{Cl_2}$, which liberates $\mathrm{I_2}$ from KI (blue with starch): Y $= \mathrm{Cl_2}$.
Answer (C).

questions.text:
Plotting $1/\Lambda_{\mathrm m}$ against $c\Lambda_{\mathrm m}$ for aqueous solutions of a monobasic weak acid (HX) resulted in a straight line with y-axis intercept of P and slope of S. The ratio P/S is
[$\Lambda_{\mathrm m}$ = molar conductivity, $\Lambda_{\mathrm m}^{\mathrm o}$ = limiting molar conductivity, c = molar concentration, $\mathrm{K_a}$ = dissociation constant of HX]
questions.sol:
With $\alpha = \dfrac{\Lambda_{\mathrm m}}{\Lambda_{\mathrm m}^{\mathrm o}}$ and $K_a = \dfrac{c\alpha^2}{1-\alpha}$: $K_a(1-\alpha) = c\alpha^2$.
$K_a\left(1 - \dfrac{\Lambda_{\mathrm m}}{\Lambda_{\mathrm m}^{\mathrm o}}\right) = \dfrac{c\Lambda_{\mathrm m}^2}{(\Lambda_{\mathrm m}^{\mathrm o})^2}$; divide by $K_a\Lambda_{\mathrm m}$: $\dfrac{1}{\Lambda_{\mathrm m}} = \dfrac{1}{\Lambda_{\mathrm m}^{\mathrm o}} + \dfrac{c\Lambda_{\mathrm m}}{K_a(\Lambda_{\mathrm m}^{\mathrm o})^2}$.
$P = \dfrac{1}{\Lambda_{\mathrm m}^{\mathrm o}}$, $S = \dfrac{1}{K_a(\Lambda_{\mathrm m}^{\mathrm o})^2}$, so $\dfrac PS = K_a\Lambda_{\mathrm m}^{\mathrm o}$. Answer (A).

questions.text: On decreasing the $p$H from 7 to 2, the solubility of a sparingly soluble salt (MX) of a weak acid (HX) increased from $10^{-4}\ \text{mol L}^{-1}$ to $10^{-3}\ \text{mol L}^{-1}$. The $p\mathrm{K_a}$ of HX is
questions.sol:
With hydrolysis of $\mathrm{X^-}$ by acid: $s^2 = K_{sp}\left(1 + \dfrac{[\mathrm{H^+}]}{K_a}\right)$.
At pH 7 the bracket is $\approx 1$, so $K_{sp} = 10^{-8}$.
At pH 2: $10^{-6} = 10^{-8}\left(1 + \dfrac{10^{-2}}{K_a}\right) \Rightarrow \dfrac{10^{-2}}{K_a} = 99 \Rightarrow K_a \approx 10^{-4}$.
$p\mathrm{K_a} = 4$. Answer (B).

questions.text: In the given reaction scheme, $\mathbf{P}$ is a phenyl alkyl ether, $\mathbf{Q}$ is an aromatic compound; $\mathbf{R}$ and $\mathbf{S}$ are the major products.$$\mathbf{P} \xrightarrow{\text{HI}} \mathbf{Q} \xrightarrow[\text{(iii) }\mathrm{H_3O^+}]{\text{(i) NaOH; (ii) }\mathrm{CO_2}} \mathbf{R} \xrightarrow[\text{(ii) }\mathrm{H_3O^+}]{\text{(i) }\mathrm{(CH_3CO)_2O}} \mathbf{S}$$The correct statement about $\mathbf{S}$ is
options: It primarily inhibits noradrenaline degrading enzymes.
It inhibits the synthesis of prostaglandin.
questions.sol:
HI cleaves the phenyl alkyl ether to phenol (Q).
Kolbe reaction (NaOH, $\mathrm{CO_2}$, then acid) gives salicylic acid (R).
Acetylation of the OH gives acetylsalicylic acid, aspirin (S): a non-narcotic analgesic that inhibits prostaglandin synthesis. It is 2-acetoxybenzoic acid, not ortho-acetylbenzoic acid.
Answer (B).

questions.text:
The stoichiometric reaction of $516$ g of dimethyldichlorosilane with water results in a tetrameric cyclic product $\mathbf{X}$ in $75\%$ yield. The weight (in g) of $\mathbf{X}$ obtained is ______.
[Use, molar mass (g $\text{mol}^{-1}$): H = 1, C = 12, O = 16, Si = 28, Cl = 35.5]
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{(CH_3)_2SiCl_2}$: $M = 30 + 28 + 71 = 129$, so $516$ g $= 4$ mol.
Hydrolysis and condensation: $\mathrm{4(CH_3)_2SiCl_2 + 4H_2O \to [(CH_3)_2SiO]_4 + 8HCl}$, giving $1$ mol of the cyclic tetramer.
$M(\mathbf X) = 4\times74 = 296$; at $75\%$ yield: $0.75\times296 = 222$ g.

questions.text:
A gas has a compressibility factor of $0.5$ and a molar volume of $0.4\ \text{dm}^3\,\text{mol}^{-1}$ at a temperature of $800$ K and pressure $\mathbf{x}$ atm. If it shows ideal gas behaviour at the same temperature and pressure, the molar volume will be $\mathbf{y}\ \text{dm}^3\,\text{mol}^{-1}$. The value of $\mathbf{x/y}$ is ______.
[Use: Gas constant, $R = 8\times10^{-2}\ \text{L atm K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$]
questions.sol:
$Z = \dfrac{PV_m}{RT}$: $0.5 = \dfrac{x\times0.4}{0.08\times800} \Rightarrow x = 80$ atm.
Ideal: $y = \dfrac{RT}{P} = \dfrac{64}{80} = 0.8\ \text{dm}^3\,\text{mol}^{-1}$.
$\dfrac xy = \dfrac{80}{0.8} = 100$.

questions.text:
The plot of $\log k_f$ versus $1/T$ for a reversible reaction $\mathrm{A(g) \rightleftharpoons P(g)}$ is shown.
Pre-exponential factors for the forward and backward reactions are $10^{15}\ \text{s}^{-1}$ and $10^{11}\ \text{s}^{-1}$, respectively. If the value of $\log K$ for the reaction at $500$ K is $6$, the value of $|\log k_b|$ at $250$ K is ______.
[$K$ = equilibrium constant of the reaction, $k_f$ = rate constant of forward reaction, $k_b$ = rate constant of backward reaction]
questions.sol:
At $500$ K ($1/T = 0.002$) the graph gives $\log k_f = 9$.
$K = \dfrac{k_f}{k_b} \Rightarrow \log k_b = 9 - 6 = 3$ at $500$ K.
$\log k_b = 11 - \dfrac{E_b}{2.303RT}$: $3 = 11 - \dfrac{E_b}{2.303R}(0.002) \Rightarrow \dfrac{E_b}{2.303R} = 4000$ K.
At $250$ K: $\log k_b = 11 - \dfrac{4000}{250} = -5$, so $|\log k_b| = 5$.

questions.text:
One mole of an ideal monoatomic gas undergoes two reversible processes ($\mathrm{A \to B}$ and $\mathrm{B \to C}$) as shown in the given figure:
$\mathrm{A \to B}$ is an adiabatic process. If the total heat absorbed in the entire process ($\mathrm{A \to B}$ and $\mathrm{B \to C}$) is $RT_2\ln10$, the value of $2\log V_3$ is ______.
[Use, molar heat capacity of the gas at constant pressure, $C_{\mathrm{p,m}} = \dfrac52R$]
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{A \to B}$ is adiabatic ($q = 0$), so all the heat is absorbed in the isothermal $\mathrm{B \to C}$: $RT_2\ln\dfrac{V_3}{V_2} = RT_2\ln10 \Rightarrow V_3 = 10V_2$.
Adiabatic, $\gamma = \dfrac53$: $T_1V_1^{2/3} = T_2V_2^{2/3} \Rightarrow 600\times10^{2/3} = 60\,V_2^{2/3} \Rightarrow V_2^{2/3} = 10^{5/3} \Rightarrow V_2 = 10^{5/2}$.
$V_3 = 10^{7/2}$, so $2\log V_3 = 7$.

questions.text:
In a one-litre flask, 6 moles of A undergoes the reaction $\mathrm{A(g) \rightleftharpoons P(g)}$. The progress of product formation at two temperatures (in Kelvin), $T_1$ and $T_2$, is shown in the figure:
If $T_1 = 2T_2$ and $\left(\Delta G_2^{\ominus} - \Delta G_1^{\ominus}\right) = RT_2\ln x$, then the value of x is ______.
[$\Delta G_1^{\ominus}$ and $\Delta G_2^{\ominus}$ are standard Gibb’s free energy change for the reaction at temperatures $T_1$ and $T_2$, respectively.]
questions.sol:
At $T_1$: $[\mathrm P] = 4$, $[\mathrm A] = 2$, $K_1 = 2$. At $T_2$: $[\mathrm P] = 2$, $[\mathrm A] = 4$, $K_2 = \dfrac12$.
$\Delta G_1^{\ominus} = -RT_1\ln2 = -2RT_2\ln2$; $\Delta G_2^{\ominus} = -RT_2\ln\dfrac12 = RT_2\ln2$.
$\Delta G_2^{\ominus} - \Delta G_1^{\ominus} = 3RT_2\ln2 = RT_2\ln8$, so $x = 8$.

questions.text:
The total number of $sp^2$ hybridised carbon atoms in the major product $\mathbf{P}$ (a non-heterocyclic compound) of the following reaction is ______.
[Reagents: (i) $\mathrm{LiAlH_4}$ (excess), then $\mathrm{H_2O}$; (ii) Acetophenone (excess)]
questions.sol:
The reactant is 1,1,2,2-tetracyanoethane, $\mathrm{(NC)_2CH{-}CH(CN)_2}$.
Excess $\mathrm{LiAlH_4}$ reduces all four $\mathrm{C{\equiv}N}$ to $\mathrm{CH_2NH_2}$: $\mathrm{(H_2NCH_2)_2CH{-}CH(CH_2NH_2)_2}$.
Each $\mathrm{NH_2}$ condenses with acetophenone to an imine $\mathrm{{-}CH_2N{=}C(CH_3)Ph}$ (four imines; the product is acyclic, not heterocyclic).
$sp^2$ carbons per imine unit: $1$ (C=N) $+ 6$ (phenyl) $= 7$; total $4\times7 = 28$.

questions.text:
Match the reactions (in the given stoichiometry of the reactants) in List-I with one of their products given in List-II and choose the correct option.
List-IList-II
(P) $\mathrm{P_2O_3 + 3H_2O \to}$(1) $\mathrm{P(O)(OCH_3)Cl_2}$
(Q) $\mathrm{P_4 + 3NaOH + 3H_2O \to}$(2) $\mathrm{H_3PO_3}$
(R) $\mathrm{PCl_5 + CH_3COOH \to}$(3) $\mathrm{PH_3}$
(S) $\mathrm{H_3PO_2 + 2H_2O + 4AgNO_3 \to}$(4) $\mathrm{POCl_3}$
(5) $\mathrm{H_3PO_4}$
questions.sol:
(P) $\mathrm{P_2O_3 + 3H_2O \to 2H_3PO_3}$ → (2).
(Q) $\mathrm{P_4 + 3NaOH + 3H_2O \to PH_3 + 3NaH_2PO_2}$ → (3).
(R) $\mathrm{PCl_5 + CH_3COOH \to CH_3COCl + POCl_3 + HCl}$ → (4).
(S) $\mathrm{H_3PO_2 + 2H_2O + 4AgNO_3 \to H_3PO_4 + 4Ag + 4HNO_3}$ → (5).
Answer (D).

questions.text:
Match the electronic configurations in List-I with appropriate metal complex ions in List-II and choose the correct option.
[Atomic Number: Fe = 26, Mn = 25, Co = 27]
List-IList-II
(P) $t_{2g}^6\,e_g^0$(1) $\mathrm{[Fe(H_2O)_6]^{2+}}$
(Q) $t_{2g}^3\,e_g^2$(2) $\mathrm{[Mn(H_2O)_6]^{2+}}$
(R) $e^2\,t_2^3$(3) $\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}}$
(S) $t_{2g}^4\,e_g^2$(4) $\mathrm{[FeCl_4]^-}$
(5) $\mathrm{[CoCl_4]^{2-}}$
questions.sol:
(P) Low-spin $d^6$ octahedral: $\mathrm{Co^{3+}}$ with strong-field $\mathrm{NH_3}$, $\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}}$ → (3).
(Q) High-spin $d^5$ octahedral: $\mathrm{Mn^{2+}}$ with weak-field water → (2).
(R) Tetrahedral $d^5$ ($e^2t_2^3$): $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$ in $\mathrm{[FeCl_4]^-}$ → (4). ($\mathrm{[CoCl_4]^{2-}}$ is $d^7$: $e^4t_2^3$.)
(S) High-spin $d^6$ octahedral: $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$ in $\mathrm{[Fe(H_2O)_6]^{2+}}$ → (1).
Answer (D).

questions.text:
Match the reactions in List-I with the features of their products in List-II and choose the correct option.
List-IList-II
(P) (-)-1-Bromo-2-ethylpentane (single enantiomer) $\xrightarrow[\mathrm{S_N2}\text{ reaction}]{\text{aq. NaOH}}$(1) Inversion of configuration
(Q) (-)-2-Bromopentane (single enantiomer) $\xrightarrow[\mathrm{S_N2}\text{ reaction}]{\text{aq. NaOH}}$(2) Retention of configuration
(R) (-)-3-Bromo-3-methylhexane (single enantiomer) $\xrightarrow[\mathrm{S_N1}\text{ reaction}]{\text{aq. NaOH}}$(3) Mixture of enantiomers
(S) The compound shown in the figure (single enantiomer) $\xrightarrow[\mathrm{S_N1}\text{ reaction}]{\text{aq. NaOH}}$(4) Mixture of structural isomers
(5) Mixture of diastereomers
questions.sol:
(P) $\mathrm{S_N2}$ occurs at the $\mathrm{CH_2Br}$ carbon, not at the stereocentre (C-2), so its configuration is retained → (2).
(Q) $\mathrm{S_N2}$ at the stereocentre (C-2): inversion of configuration → (1).
(R) $\mathrm{S_N1}$ at the only stereocentre: the planar carbocation is attacked from both faces, giving a racemic mixture of enantiomers → (3).
(S) $\mathrm{S_N1}$ at the C-Br stereocentre while the other stereocentre (C-Me, H) is unchanged: the two products are diastereomers → (5).
Answer (B).

The major products obtained from the reactions in List-II are the reactants for the named reactions mentioned in List-I. Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct option.
List-IList-II
(P) Etard reaction(1) Acetophenone $\xrightarrow{\text{Zn-Hg, HCl}}$
(Q) Gattermann reaction(2) Toluene $\xrightarrow[\text{(ii) }\mathrm{SOCl_2}]{\text{(i) }\mathrm{KMnO_4}\text{, KOH, }\Delta}$
(R) Gattermann-Koch reaction(3) Benzene $\xrightarrow[\text{anhyd. }\mathrm{AlCl_3}]{\mathrm{CH_3Cl}}$
(S) Rosenmund reduction(4) Aniline $\xrightarrow[\text{273-278 K}]{\mathrm{NaNO_2/HCl}}$
(5) Phenol $\xrightarrow{\text{Zn},\ \Delta}$
questions.sol:
Products of List-II: (1) ethylbenzene (Clemmensen); (2) benzoyl chloride; (3) toluene; (4) benzenediazonium chloride; (5) benzene.
(P) Etard reaction oxidises toluene to benzaldehyde → (3).
(Q) Gattermann reaction uses a diazonium salt with Cu/HX → (4).
(R) Gattermann-Koch formylates benzene (CO, HCl) → (5).
(S) Rosenmund reduction converts an acid chloride (benzoyl chloride) to an aldehyde → (2).
Answer (D).
